root_cause.text: On UP kernels, spin_trylock() always succeeds even if the lock is already held, so kmalloc_nolock() called from NMI context can re-enter the slab allocator and acquire n->list_lock that the interrupted context holds, corrupting slab state.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "On UP kernels (!CONFIG_SMP), spin_trylock() is a no-op that unconditionally succeeds even when the lock is already held. As a result, kmalloc_nolock() called from NMI context can re-enter the slab allocator and acquire n->list_lock that the interrupted context is already holding, corrupting slab state." The patch adds `if (!IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_SMP) && in_nmi()) return NULL;` to prevent this re-entry.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a potential lock corruption on UP systems by returning NULL from kmalloc_nolock_noprof when in NMI context, because spin_trylock always succeeds on UP even if the lock is held.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check in kmalloc_nolock_noprof that returns NULL if CONFIG_SMP is disabled and the current context is NMI, with a comment explaining the spin_trylock behavior on UP.
intent_record.how: When running on a uniprocessor (UP) kernel, the function now immediately returns NULL if called from NMI context, preventing the use of spin_trylock which would incorrectly succeed on UP and potentially corrupt a held lock.

grouping_result.intent: Fix a potential lock corruption on UP systems by returning NULL from kmalloc_nolock_noprof when in NMI context, because spin_trylock always succeeds on UP even if the lock is held.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the vulnerability described: it prevents re-entering the slab allocator from NMI context on UP systems by returning NULL, addressing the spin_trylock always succeeding issue.

candidates.rationale: On UP kernels without PREEMPT_RT, spin_trylock always succeeds even if the lock is held. This condition only guards against re-entry in NMI/hardirq when PREEMPT_RT is enabled, leaving UP vulnerable to slab corruption when kmalloc_nolock_noprof is called from NMI context.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition only guards against re-entry in NMI/hardirq when PREEMPT_RT is enabled. On UP kernels without PREEMPT_RT, spin_trylock always succeeds even if the lock is held, so kmalloc_nolock_noprof can be called from NMI context and corrupt the slab state by acquiring n->list_lock that the interrupted context holds.
